answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that Player ID card upright in its plastic stand in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set whose backs match that color, remove cards targeting colors not in the game, and keep their own Ambush card. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “upright in their plastic stand”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player voting turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. After everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is required. Red is a Target because Red received the most votes; the Target is the player receiving the most votes, even when that is only a plurality.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, provided they are not themselves eliminated as a Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; with tied Targets, “voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: every player who did not vote for any Target is eliminated, unless protected by the successful Ambush exception. Green voted for Red, not the sole Target Blue, and did not Ambush.
answers.evidence: Resolve elimination: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated,” subject to the successful Ambush exception.

answers.answer: Ambush does not count as a vote. Yellow’s vote for Red and Pink’s vote for Yellow are one vote each, so Red and Yellow tie for the most votes and both are Targets. Red’s Ambush succeeds and Red survives; Red may retaliate against Yellow, who voted for Red, eliminating Yellow. Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: Three-player illustration: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes Red, Pink votes Yellow; Red and Yellow tie as Targets; “Yellow is eliminated; Red survives” and Pink survives by voting for tied Target Yellow.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets the player choose exactly one player who voted for them to eliminate, even if four players voted for them. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “chooses one of the players who voted for them”; “They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, continue with another conspiracy and vote among those surviving players.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Three or more — Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors”; resolve the round after the vote and Ambush effects.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “One — That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; they may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down. When both are ready, they reveal their choices simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes a set of “Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; discuss, choose face down, then “reveal both choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive none for this outcome, including those eliminated in it. Leave the four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.” Special Rules clarifies final voters receive no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown payoff table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share player receives zero bars and the Steal player receives all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown payoff table, Share versus Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one bar and the Steal player receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: Grab One & Go against Steal gives Grab One & Go player 1 and opponent 3; “Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one bar and the Share player receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: Grab One & Go against Share gives Grab One & Go player 1 and opponent 3; “Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.”

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two bars remain in the center, and if play continues, deal just two new central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each receive one central bar”; “Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Check victory at the end of the round, after Gold Bars are awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: check “at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; “the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: The tied qualifying leaders conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: tied highest qualifying totals “conduct another Final Showdown” and “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: if there is no winner, “everyone returns.”
